analysis.title: CIO View: US Equities
key_insights: UBS CIO keeps an Attractive absolute view on US equities and a Neutral relative preference versus other equity regions. The S&P 500 is near record highs despite rising interest rates.
Higher rates have pressured valuations, but earnings growth has been solid and the forward 12-month EPS estimate keeps rising.

UBS says the bull market remains intact, driven by a resilient US economy with strong profit growth and by AI investment and adoption. Monetary policy is no longer a tailwind, and UBS does not expect the Fed to hike enough to become a meaningful headwind, though this bears watching.
S&P 500 targets are 8,100 for December 2026 and 8,400 for June 2027. The index was 7,713 on 20 Oct 2026. S&P 500 EPS is expected to grow 25% to USD 350 in 2026 and 14% to USD 400 in 2027.
US GDP grew near 2.5% annualized in the first half of 2026, and 3Q growth is tracking near 3%. Consumer spending is resilient and the labor market is healthy.

3Q earnings season is underway. UBS expects solid results and guidance, with corporate profits likely up 28% y/y on a typical level of beats. Earnings growth is decelerating, which likely means a slower pace of equity gains and a bias toward high-quality companies.

AI-related spending is expected to account for about 60% of S&P 500 earnings growth, and that share is likely to rise next year. Hyperscaler capex (Alphabet, Meta, Microsoft, Amazon) is expected to rise 84% in 2026 and 33% in 2027.
Cloud providers' aggregate revenue grew 48% in 2Q, the highest in seven years. Consensus estimates suggest further acceleration in 3Q.
UBS economists expect 25 bp Fed rate hikes at both the December 2026 and March 2027 FOMC meetings, following hotter-than-expected recent inflation prints.

UBS argues higher rates should not be a major headwind for S&P 500 profits because refinancing risk is manageable. Housing will weaken but is already muted, hyperscaler capex is less rate sensitive, and the labor market is not a source of inflation, unlike in 2022.
UBS does not expect the midterm election results to have much policy impact. It thinks the 2028 presidential election is too early to drive sustained market moves.
Attractive sectors are consumer discretionary, financials, health care, industrials and utilities.

Upside (Goldilocks) scenario has a June 2027 S&P 500 target of 9,500. It assumes AI spending and adoption beat expectations, a quick reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, a Russia-Ukraine ceasefire, and the effective US tariff rate falling below 10%.

Downside (AI bear market) scenario has a June 2027 S&P 500 target of 5,500. It assumes AI stocks deflate over weak returns on investment and unsustainable commitments, US growth weakens, and central banks cut rates aggressively in 2027.

sector_views.rationale: Consumer spending should remain resilient. Year-to-date increases and volatility in energy prices are manageable unless prices spike to new highs.

Improving profitability metrics, easing regulations and strong capital markets activity support steady earnings growth. Payments transaction volumes remain supportive and recent credit trends suggest broad stability.
UBS sees no near-term catalyst for negative health care policies but is watching the policy backdrop ahead of the midterms. Valuations have crept higher, which UBS says appears warranted.
Favorable ISM Manufacturing readings add confidence in a cyclical manufacturing upcycle, and the sector has exposure to attractive secular themes.
Defensive characteristics offer ballast if growth slows further. Roughly 25% of the sector has material exposure to AI power demand.

earnings_insights: 3Q 2026 S&P 500 corporate profits are expected to have grown 28% y/y (UBS estimate), reflecting a typical level of earnings beats. Earnings growth is decelerating.
S&P 500 EPS forecast (UBS estimate): USD 350 in 2026 (+25%) and USD 400 in 2027 (+14%).
Cloud providers' aggregate revenue grew 48% in 2Q (reported), the highest in seven years. Consensus estimates suggest further acceleration in 3Q.
AI-related spending is estimated to account for about 60% of S&P 500 earnings growth (UBS estimate).

macro_indicators.interpretation: Supports the view of a resilient US economy and earnings growth.
Tracking estimate at the time of writing. It shows good cyclical momentum and supports the earnings outlook.

macro_indicators.reading: 25 bp hike expected at both the December 2026 and March 2027 FOMC meetings
macro_indicators.interpretation: Hotter-than-expected inflation prints are pushing rates higher. UBS expects no aggressive hiking because the labor market is not driving inflation.
UBS base-case targets, above the 7,713 level on 20 Oct 2026.
Adds confidence in a cyclical manufacturing upcycle, supporting the industrials view.
A more benign tariff policy is a condition of the Goldilocks scenario.

risk_factors: Fed hiking enough for monetary policy to become a meaningful headwind. UBS says this bears watching.
Decelerating earnings growth, which likely means slower equity gains if earnings revisions stop being supportive.
An AI setback from low returns on investment and unsustainable commitments by large AI companies, which could broaden into a market decline.
Higher rates weighing on housing activity.
Energy price spikes to new highs would challenge the consumer discretionary view.
Health care policy risk around the US midterm elections.
Inflation concerns turning into fears of a global economic decline.
geopolitical: A quick reopening of the Strait of Hormuz with clear signs of accelerating transit activity is part of the upside scenario.
A Russia-Ukraine ceasefire agreement is part of the upside scenario.
US midterm elections are not expected to have much policy impact, and UBS thinks the 2028 presidential election is too early to drive sustained market moves.
Trade agreements and carve-outs lowering the effective US tariff rate below 10% are part of the upside scenario.

tension_points.bull_case: AI investment is the largest source of S&P 500 earnings growth, at about 60%. Hyperscaler capex is forecast up 84% in 2026, and cloud revenue grew 48% in 2Q, which suggests the spending is paying off.
tension_points.bear_case: In the downside scenario, concerns over low returns on investment and unsustainable commitments by large AI companies deflate AI stocks, drag the broader market and take the S&P 500 to 5,500 by June 2027.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Declining AI infrastructure investment or worsening investor sentiment on AI returns, which is the trigger for the downside scenario.

tension_points.bull_case: UBS expects only 25 bp hikes in December 2026 and March 2027. Refinancing risk is manageable, hyperscaler capex is less rate sensitive, and the labor market is not driving inflation, so there is no urgency to hike aggressively.
tension_points.bear_case: Higher rates have already pressured valuations and no longer provide a tailwind. A Fed that hikes enough would make monetary policy a meaningful headwind, which UBS says bears watching.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The Fed hiking by enough to make monetary policy a meaningful headwind, for example more aggressive hikes after further hot inflation prints.
